about: MobaLedLib hardware modules for a chain view. Not from the Excel workbook: a deliberate exception, the facts come from wiki.mobaledlib.de (source per module). Nothing here changes LEDs_AutoProg.h. 'unconfirmed' lists what no source confirms yet. Ports are the data-port ids in the SVG. 'leds' is how many LED numbers the module takes in the chain, 'channels' how many single outputs (3 per WS2811).

modules.name: LichtMaschine Classic (101)
facts: 2 LED channels, numbered 0 and 2, each fused at 1 A
each channel has a heartbeat LED at its output and one at its input
768 single LEDs or 256 RGB LEDs; DCC, CAN, LNet, Selectrix
unconfirmed: pin count of each connector (the wiki lists 3x 6-pin, 2x 8-pin, 1x 14-pin)
whether the heartbeat LEDs take LED numbers in the chain
DCC and power terminals are not drawn

modules.name: Universal Verteiler Pro (201)
facts: 12 outputs plus 'Next' to the next splitter; 'Next' is the last channel and has no DIP switch
a 12-way DIP switch bridges each unused output
two WS2812 amplify the signal: FWD at the input, BACK in the return path
the input LED is defined first, the return LED at the end of the chain or of each branch
separate 5V and 12V terminals, at most 2.5 A per voltage; flat cables are rated at 1 A
between splitters, chain only 4-pole cables (data only, no power)
unconfirmed: the connector pinout is taken from the 200 page; the 201 page says its connectors follow the 200
the 5V/12V power terminals are not drawn

modules.name: WS2811 Multi-Use v2 (503)
facts: 12 WS2811F chips (v1 had 10), 3 outputs each: up to 36 single LEDs; can also feed series circuits on 12 V
three sections that can be cut apart
when nothing follows, solder jumpers T1/T2/T3 loop the signal back to the input: T2 if section 3 is cut off, T1 if sections 2 and 3 are cut off
unconfirmed: 4 chips per section (12 chips in 3 equal sections)
positions of the pads and of T1-T3

modules.name: WS2811 Multi-Use Micro (504)
facts: 2 WS2811F chips: six single LEDs, three of them sharing each plus pole
pad layout like a WS2812B (+5V, data in/out, GND), so it can replace a WS2812B in a chain
up to about 1 A on its supply tracks

modules.name: 24-Single LED Connector v2 (521)
facts: 8 WS2811F chips: up to 24 single LEDs
6-pin input and output; the 'Term' jumper in the output loops the signal back to the splitter
separate 5V and 12V terminals; two-pole 12 V outputs for series circuits
unused chips must be reserved with 'Reserve LEDs'
24 x 18.5 mA = about 444 mA at full brightness
unconfirmed: outputs 13-24 on the upper terminal row

modules.name: TinyHouse (295)
facts: six single LED outputs (LED1, LED2: R+, G+, B+), 5V or 12V per group of three by a solder jumper
three RGB outputs (LED3-LED5: 5V, GND, data in/out), each with a solder jumper (NoLED, Skip4+5, ...); a jumper disables all following outputs, so fill them from right to left
an onboard RGB heartbeat LED at the end of the data bus
unconfirmed: number of LED numbers taken (depends on what is connected to LED3-LED5)
the vertical pin row next to the input (5V DI GN DO GN 12V) is not drawn

modules.name: WS2811 breakout
facts: single WorldSemi WS2811B board, 5 V, sold as a breakaway panel of 10 x 10
front: LED pads B, G, +, R (left, top to bottom); +, DO, - (right)
unconfirmed: where DI is (not on the front; probably the back)
which pad gets which byte of the LED (some WS2811 variants use G-R-B order)

modules.name: WS2812
facts: RGB LED with an integrated WS2811 chip; three constant-current outputs of 18.5 mA

modules.name: Single LED
facts: a plain LED on one WS2811 output; takes no LED number of its own

modules.name: Lamp
facts: one WS2811 output; lit through the CSS variables --lamp-color and --lamp-level (0..1)

modules.name: RGB lamp
facts: a plain RGB LED on the three outputs of one WS2811; lit through the CSS variables --r, --g, --b (0..255)
